correctness.rationale: For white support in at least two parts, the white induced graph is connected and the exact white-neighbor count of a blue vertex in part i is the sum of white occupancies outside i. This gives a necessary and sufficient first-force condition; after that force, only one white part remains. The enumerator follows by disjoint support-size cases with a single explicit double-count correction. A direct exhaustive implementation agrees with the criterion on 182540 initial sets across 269 profiles and agrees coefficient-by-coefficient with the formula.

originality.rationale: Peters gives the complete multipartite scalar PSD zero forcing number but not the set-level characterization or cardinality enumerator. The ordinary zero forcing polynomial literature uses a different forcing rule. Targeted searches for PSD/positive semidefinite forcing sets, polynomials, minimum sets, and reconfiguration on complete multipartite graphs did not reveal a statement implying the all-set theorem.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification and exact cardinality enumerator for a canonical graph family whose PSD zero forcing minimum is already a standard benchmark. It strictly refines the known scalar invariant and explains the component-splitting structure that controls success, making the fact reusable for counting, random-initialization questions, and minimum-set descriptions.
